title: Upgrade telemetry: step metrics + structured logs + diagnostics bundle export
creator: Sean Gallagher
content:
Goal
Provide end-to-end observability for Private upgrades/rollbacks so SRE/Support can answer:
- What step are we on? (and which component)
- How long is it taking vs expected?
- Why did we fail? (with remediation hints)
- Can we correlate installer output to control plane + cluster events?
- Can we export a single diagnostics artifact for escalation?

Scope
- Installer emits structured logs for every upgrade step (prechecks, backup, apply, gates, smoke test, rollback hooks).
- Prometheus metrics emitted during upgrade/rollback runs (step duration, failure counts, state).
- Correlation ID generated at the start of a run and propagated:
  - installer logs
  - upgrade controller/control plane logs (where available)
  - diagnostics bundle metadata
- Exportable diagnostics bundle (tar.gz) that can be attached to Support tickets.

Non-goals
- Building a full "upgrade UI" in Console (this is CLI-first for v1).
- Replacing existing cluster observability stacks; we integrate with the existing observability pack where present.

Motivation / Background
Upgrade safety is only as good as our ability to detect regressions and triage failures quickly. Beta feedback so far: operators can see "something failed" but spend 30–60 minutes collecting K8s events, pod logs, and figuring out which step they were actually on. We need deterministic step-level telemetry and a standardized diagnostics bundle.

Requirements
1) Structured logs (installer)
- Format: JSON lines to stdout/stderr when run with --log-format=json (default remains human-friendly text).
- Each step MUST emit:
  - timestamp
  - level (debug|info|warn|error)
  - run_id (UUID)
  - step_id (stable identifier, e.g., "backup.controlplane_db")
  - step_name (human readable)
  - attempt (int)
  - status (started|succeeded|failed|skipped|aborted)
  - duration_ms (on terminal events)
  - component (control-plane|gateway|runtime|observability|installer)
  - target_version + from_version (when relevant)
  - error_code (stable string, e.g., "SNAPSHOT_PERMISSION_DENIED")
  - remediation (short operator hint; safe for customer visibility)
  - links (optional string; e.g., runbook anchor or docs URL)
- Redaction: never log secrets (kubeconfig tokens, DB credentials, cloud credentials). Any structured log field that may contain sensitive values must be either omitted or replaced with "[REDACTED]".

2) Metrics (upgrade runs)
- Exposed via existing metrics endpoint when observability pack is installed; otherwise written to a local file in the diagnostics bundle.
- Metric namespace: redwood_private_upgrade_*
- Required metrics:
  - redwood_private_upgrade_run_started_total{mode="upgrade|rollback", trigger="manual|auto"}
  - redwood_private_upgrade_run_completed_total{mode, result="success|failure|aborted"}
  - redwood_private_upgrade_step_duration_seconds_bucket{step_id, component, result}
  - redwood_private_upgrade_step_failures_total{step_id, component, error_code}
  - redwood_private_upgrade_current_step{step_id, component} (gauge; last known step)
  - redwood_private_upgrade_state{state="idle|running|rolling_back|completed"} (gauge)
  - redwood_private_upgrade_artifact_verification_failures_total{reason}
- Cardinality constraints:
  - step_id is bounded by the finite step graph
  - error_code must be from a short allowlist
  - do not include customer-specific identifiers as labels

3) Correlation ID (run_id)
- Installer generates run_id at invocation. Persist to disk so retries can continue the same run_id when invoked with --resume.
- Installer must pass run_id to control plane upgrade APIs (if/when used) and include it as an HTTP header: X-Redwood-Upgrade-Run-Id.
- Control plane should log run_id on receipt and include in audit events for upgrade/rollback actions.
- Diagnostics bundle must include run_id in a top-level manifest.

4) Diagnostics bundle
- Command: redwood-private-installer diagnostics export --run-id <id> [--output <path>]
- Also automatically emitted on failure (with a clear path printed).
- Bundle name: redwood-private-diagnostics_<cluster>_<run_id>_<timestamp>.tar.gz
- Contents (minimum viable):
  - manifest.json (version, run_id, installer_version, target_version, mode, timestamps, platform="vpc|onprem")
  - prechecks.json (from ENG-2316)
  - upgrade_plan.json (step graph + resolved versions)
  - step_report.json (per-step status + durations + error_code + remediation)
  - installer.log (raw text output)
  - installer.jsonl (structured logs if enabled)
  - kubernetes/
    - events.txt (kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.lastTimestamp)
    - pods_wide.txt (kubectl get pods -A -o wide)
    - nodes.txt (kubectl get nodes -o wide)
    - describe/ (describe for failing pods, bounded)
    - logs/ (bounded; last N lines for pods matching label selectors)
  - versions.txt (component versions detected)
  - backup/ (backup step output metadata only; no snapshot payloads)
  - redaction_report.txt (what was redacted; counts only)
- Size constraints:
  - hard cap default 250MB; truncate logs with clear markers
  - allow operator overrides: --max-bytes, --max-log-lines

Acceptance Criteria
- For a full upgrade run in staging, we can answer within 5 minutes:
  - which step failed
  - how long each step took
  - whether rollback was triggered and why
  - link to relevant runbook remediation section
- Support can request a single bundle from customer and have:
  - precheck output
  - step timing/failures
  - key cluster snapshots (events, pods)
  - run_id that matches control plane logs/audit events
- Metrics available in Grafana dashboard (observability pack) and alerting hooks defined (SRE will set final thresholds in runbook).
- Security review sign-off on redaction and bundle contents.

Implementation Plan
- Installer:
  - Introduce RunContext (run_id, mode, start_time, env, versions)
  - StepRunner emits structured events on start/end
  - Standardize error codes and remediation strings in step definitions
  - Diagnostics collector with bounded collection and redaction filters
- Control plane integration:
  - Add header propagation to upgrade API calls
  - Ensure audit log event includes run_id (coordinate with control plane owners)
- Observability pack:
  - Add dashboard panels for: step duration p50/p95, failure rate, run completion results, and current step gauge
  - Add alerts: upgrade failure rate > X in Y; step duration > threshold for key steps (backup, migration)

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - structured log schema validator
  - error_code allowlist enforced
  - redaction tests (known secret patterns)
- Integration tests:
  - run a simulated upgrade with injected failure (disk full / snapshot permission denied)
  - verify diagnostics bundle is generated and contains expected files
  - verify metrics exported (or written to bundle when metrics endpoint absent)

Open Questions
- Where do we store a durable pointer to "latest diagnostics bundle" for a given run_id in air-gapped on-prem? Proposal: local filesystem under /var/lib/redwood/diagnostics with operator-controlled rotation.
- Do we want installer to auto-upload diagnostics to customer-controlled object store in VPC mode? Likely v2; v1 stays local export with optional manual upload.

Links
- Related work: correlation id propagation in control plane logs (see control plane PR referenced by Release Eng)
- Observability pack dashboard/alerts PR will be separate but tracked under this ticket until merged.
comments: 2025-01-23 (Allison Grant): Drafted metrics names and initial JSON log schema. Need SRE feedback on which steps warrant alerts (backup + migration + gateway rollout?).

2025-01-28 (Aisha Bello): Please keep label cardinality tight; do NOT include cluster_id/customer_id as a Prometheus label. Step_id + error_code allowlist is fine. Also add a gauge for current state so dashboards can show when a run is active.

2025-02-02 (Jacob Stein): Diagnostics bundle should include: kubectl get events, pods wide, and last N lines for pods in namespaces: redwood-system, redwood-runtime. Recommend 2k lines per pod by default; add caps to avoid 1GB bundles.

2025-02-06 (Marcus Lin): Security review note: bundle must never include kubeconfig or cloud credentials; redact env vars in pod logs if we capture them indirectly. Provide a redaction report for auditability (counts + patterns used).

2025-02-14 (Rafael Mendes): Runbook alignment: error_code strings should map 1:1 to runbook sections. If the remediation hint is short, add a link field to the exact anchor in the runbook so on-call can jump quickly.

2025-02-21 (Allison Grant): Implemented RunContext + step lifecycle events in installer; added bounded diagnostics collector (max bytes + max log lines). Remaining: wire correlation header to control plane requests and finish Grafana dashboard panels in observability pack.

2025-03-03 (Sean Gallagher): Did a rehearsal in staging. Bundle generation works; size was ~140MB. Biggest issue: we weren’t capturing describe output for the failing migration job pod. Please add targeted describe collection for pods in Failed/CrashLoopBackOff.
2025-03-07 (Allison Grant): Added targeted describe for failing pods and tightened redaction. Marking In Review pending Security final sign-off and SRE dashboard review.
